description: verify_bundle strict mode: producer signatures, the signed checkpoint, producer-selected Bundles, the disclosures claim and witness receipts. See README.md.

cases.description: Three signed records, a whole-log certificate, a signed COSE checkpoint; no receipts.
The records' key is the checkpoint's key: reported, never gating.
No checkpoint.cose: the checkpoint is not shown, so neither are the proofs under it.
The JSON copy's timestamp differs from the signed statement's.
prev_size is JSON false where the signed statement says 0: a different value.
The JSON copy has no log_id.
The last byte of the COSE checkpoint's signature is flipped.
checkpoint.cose is not unpadded base64url.
The second record carries no producer signature.
The same Bundle, checked with require_signature.
The first record's envelope is signed by another key than its key_id.
The third record's content is edited after signing: identity, signature, closure and membership fail.
Records 1 and 3 of the log, producer-selected: the interval is not checkable, each record's proof is.
The same, with the third record's inclusion proof edited.
Producer-selected: the certificate's log_id is not the signed one, though the checkpoint's copy is.
Producer-selected: the certificate's and the checkpoint's log_id both name another log; one mismatch.
Producer-selected: the certificate's log_id is null and the checkpoint carries none.
Producer-selected: one membership names another log, another has seq 0.
Producer-selected: leaf_index is not seq - 1.
Producer-selected: two memberships claim seq 1.
Producer-selected: a record's membership has no coordinates.
The checkpoint follows a prior one after two records and carries the consistency proof (prev_size > 0).
The first checkpoint's JSON copy says prev_root null where the signed statement says "".
A disclosures overlay whose member matches the digest its record commits to.
The same overlay with the disclosed member edited.
The third record appears twice: the second copy is a record the plain verifier skipped.
bundle_kind is not evidence-bundle/v2: refused before any other strict check.
A CLL witness receipt verifies under the directory's key for it.
The same receipt with no directory: no witness is trusted.
A receipt labelled with the pre-rename grade reads as observed-only.
A receipt with no grade label verifies, with no grade.
A receipt from a witness the directory has no row for is not checked.
A directory row with no keys checks nothing.
A stub receipt never counts.
A genuine receipt for another checkpoint.
A receipt for this checkpoint signed by a key the row does not list.
A receipt whose payload is attached and signed by the listed key: not bound to the root.
A receipt over the right root whose payload is CBOR undefined (0xf7), not null: not detached.
A receipt signed over the right root that declares vds 2 (CCF).
A receipt signed over the right root that declares alg -257.
A cll receipt signed ES256 under the row's P-256 key.
A receipt declaring ES256, signed with the secp256k1 key the row lists: that key does not count, so the row's key id is read as a raw Ed25519 key and nothing verifies.
The row's key id is 32 bytes that are not an Ed25519 public key: nothing verifies under it.

The row's key is the identity point, a small-order Ed25519 key, and the receipt's signature is R = the identity, S = 0: it satisfies the cofactorless equation for any root, and strict Ed25519 refuses it.
The row's first key does not verify the receipt; its second does.
The only row for this endpoint says binding null: it is no cll row, so the receipt is not checked.
is_stub is 1, not JSON true: the entry is checked as a receipt, and its bytes are not one.
A receipt entry without tree_size, beside a good one.
A receipt entry whose receipt_b64 is empty, for a witness the directory has no row for: malformed, not merely unchecked.
Beside a good receipt, one whose receipt_b64 is not canonical base64 and one whose entry_hash is not a string.
Beside a good receipt: a non-string ts_url, an empty entry_hash, a receipt_b64 with a line break, one without its padding, and a stub with an empty receipt_b64.
A SCRAPI receipt over SHA-256 of the COSE checkpoint, no grade label.
A SCRAPI receipt with an unknown grade label reads as observed-only.
A SCRAPI receipt over other bytes.
A Rekor dsse entry for the COSE checkpoint, logged under the checkpoint's key.
A Rekor entry whose payloadHash is other bytes.
A Rekor entry for these bytes logged under another key.
integratedTime is the signed value as a JSON string.
A rekor row listing a log ID with no public key checks nothing.
The rekor row's only public key is an RSA key: it is skipped, so the row has no key for its log ID and the receipt is not checked.
The rekor row's only public key is a well-formed key under an unknown algorithm: it is skipped, so the row has no key for its log ID and the receipt is not checked.
One receipt of each binding, all verifying.
A cll receipt whose witness signed iat into its protected header, in the checkpoint's own second: the receipt's registration time is that iat.
A receipt whose signed iat is 90 seconds after the checkpoint's timestamp: the registration time is the iat, never the checkpoint's timestamp.
A receipt with a signed iat and no directory: it is not checked, so it has no registration time.
A receipt with an iat, signed by a key the row does not list: it fails, so it has no registration time.
A receipt with no protected iat whose unprotected header carries one: no signature covers it, so the receipt has no registration time.
A receipt whose signed iat is a float: the receipt verifies, and its iat is no registration time.
A receipt whose protected CWT claims (label 15) are an integer, not a map: no registration time.
A receipt whose signed iat is 2^53, past the largest integer every language reads exactly.
A receipt whose protected CWT claims key a time by the float 6.0: that is no iat claim.
A SCRAPI receipt with a signed iat.
checkpoint.cose is JSON null: the strict checkpoint claim reads it as absent; the plain verifier's proof claims refuse it as an authenticator that is present but not a string.
Receipts are never checked against a checkpoint that is not signed.

record_signatures.description: A format-4 record signed by its key_id.
A vintage record with no canonicalization_id: jcs-n drops chain and null or empty members.
A vintage record declaring canonicalization_id jcs-n.
Signed by another key than key_id.
signature and key_id are present as JSON null.
A canonicalization_id the Capsule ID cannot be recomputed under.
